newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark forecasts TV sport earnings.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark forecasts TV sport earnings.

text.p: Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark said on Wednesday that it expected to recover its investment in the cable tv sports broadcaster Sportskanalen within the next six to eight years.

Speaking to journalists during a media seminar, Tele Danmark director Gregers Mogensen would not say how much the group had put into Sportskanalen but said that a reported figure of 200 million crowns was "a good guess".
"It will take three or four years before Sportskanalen stops making losses and another three or four years to fill up the hole," he said.
Sportskanalen, a joint venture between Tele Danmark, state-owned Danish Radio, independent TV2 and the Danish Football Association, is due to start transmitting next March 1.

Monthly subscription charges will be about 150 crowns, to which customers will have to add the cost of decoder rental. Sportskanelen director Peter Herforth said that the service hoped to attract some 200,000 subscribers.

Tele Danmark's Bo Christensen said that the group's existing cable TV and radio delivery network for other broadcasters was expected to expand to one million households connected by the turn of the century, from 750,000 at the end of 1996.
Tele Danmark, 51 percent owned by the Danish state, last month bought into local programme provider Metronome, thereby ensuring a supply of film, music and video content.
The group's 70 percent-owned Tele Danmark Radio is on March 1 to start transmission of its Radio 2, Denmark's first national independent radio station.

Broadcast will be over Tele Danmark's existing cable network, with the addition of satellite transmission, bringing the potential total reach to 2.4 million homes. It expects actual daily listeners to the commercial station to number about 140,000 in the first year, rising to 250,000 in 1998. --Uffe Hansen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969650
